create.ponder.shaft.text_1: A Shaft passes rotation on along its own axis, block after block, in a straight line
create.ponder.shaft_casing.text_1: Put Andesite or Brass Casing on a Shaft to hide it inside a solid block; it keeps turning as before
create.ponder.cogwheel.text_1: Cogwheels that touch each other side by side pass the rotation from one to the next
create.ponder.cogwheel.text_2: Because of this, the shafts on two meshing cogs always spin in opposite directions
create.ponder.cog_speedup.text_1: A large and a small cogwheel on parallel axes mesh when placed diagonally next to each other
create.ponder.cog_speedup.text_2: Driving the small cog from the large one gives the small cog twice the speed
create.ponder.cog_speedup.text_3: Drive it the other way round, from small to large, and the speed is cut in half
create.ponder.cogwheel_casing.text_1: Cogwheels and Large Cogwheels can be wrapped in Andesite or Brass Casing too
create.ponder.cogwheel_casing.text_2: Anything you attach after encasing stays still: the casing keeps its shaft openings closed
create.ponder.cogwheel_casing.text_3: Use a Wrench on a face of the casing to open or close the shaft connection there
create.ponder.large_cogwheel.header: Relaying rotational force using Large Cogwheels
create.ponder.large_cogwheel.text_1: Two Large Cogwheels can mesh at a right angle to each other
create.ponder.large_cogwheel.text_2: This lets you carry the same speed over onto a different axis of rotation
create.ponder.belt_connector.text_1: Use a belt item on one shaft, then on a second: a belt is stretched between the two
create.ponder.belt_connector.text_2: Picked the wrong shaft? Sneak and Right-Click to drop the current selection
create.ponder.belt_connector.text_3: More shafts can be fitted into the belt anywhere along its length
create.ponder.belt_connector.text_4: Every shaft on the same belt turns at exactly the same speed and in the same direction
create.ponder.belt_connector.text_5: Take an added shaft back out by using a Wrench on it
create.ponder.belt_connector.text_6: Dyes give belts a new colour; this is purely cosmetic
create.ponder.belt_directions.text_1: A belt cannot be stretched between just any two shafts
create.ponder.belt_directions.text_3: 2. Up or down a 45 degree slope
create.ponder.belt_directions.text_5: 4. On its side, joining two upright shafts
create.ponder.belt_directions.text_6: That is the full list. A single belt may be anywhere from 2 to 20 blocks long
create.ponder.belt_transport.text_1: A running belt carries items, mobs and players along with it
create.ponder.belt_transport.text_2: Right-Click the belt with an empty hand to pick an item up from it
create.ponder.belt_casing.text_1: Andesite or Brass Casing can be put around a belt to dress it up
create.ponder.belt_casing.text_2: Use a Wrench on an encased section to take its casing off again
create.ponder.gearbox.text_1: Turning a corner with Large Cogwheels takes up a lot of room
create.ponder.gearbox.text_2: A Gearbox does the same job in a single block
create.ponder.gearbox.text_3: Shafts taken off to the sides turn as mirror images of each other
create.ponder.gearbox.text_4: A shaft straight across from the input turns the opposite way
create.ponder.clutch.header: Controlling rotational force using a Clutch
create.ponder.clutch.text_1: Unpowered, a Clutch simply passes rotation straight through like a shaft
create.ponder.clutch.text_2: A redstone signal disengages it: everything past the Clutch comes to a stop
create.ponder.gearshift.header: Controlling rotational force using a Gearshift
create.ponder.gearshift.text_1: Without a redstone signal, a Gearshift relays rotation straight through
create.ponder.gearshift.text_2: A redstone signal flips it: the output side now spins the other way
create.ponder.sequenced_gearshift.header: Controlling Rotational Speed using Sequenced Gearshifts
create.ponder.sequenced_gearshift.text_1: A Sequenced Gearshift passes rotation on by working through a timed list of steps
create.ponder.sequenced_gearshift.text_2: Right-Click it to open the screen where the steps are set up
create.ponder.sequenced_gearshift.text_3: A redstone pulse starts the sequence from the top
create.ponder.sequenced_gearshift.text_4: When the last step is done it stops and waits for the next signal to run again
create.ponder.sequenced_gearshift.text_5: A Redstone Comparator behind it outputs how far the sequence has got
create.ponder.creative_motor.header: Generating Rotational Force using Creative Motors
create.ponder.creative_motor.text_1: A Creative Motor is a small, adjustable source of rotational force
create.ponder.creative_motor.text_2: Scroll over the value panel on its side to choose the speed it produces
create.ponder.creative_motor_mojang.head: Mojang's Enigma
create.ponder.water_wheel.header: Generating Rotational Force using Water Wheels
create.ponder.water_wheel.text_1: A Water Wheel takes its power from flowing water running past it
create.ponder.water_wheel.text_2: Adding water on more sides of the wheel will not make it any stronger
create.ponder.water_wheel.text_3: Use wooden planks on the wheel to give it a different look
create.ponder.large_water_wheel.header: Generating Rotational Force using Large Water Wheels
create.ponder.large_water_wheel.text_1: Large Water Wheels are also driven by flowing water next to them
create.ponder.large_water_wheel.text_2: Putting water against further sides gains nothing extra
create.ponder.large_water_wheel.text_3: Compared to the small wheel, they turn only half as fast...
create.ponder.large_water_wheel.text_4: ...but in exchange they can carry far more stress
create.ponder.large_water_wheel.text_5: Wooden planks used on the wheel change which wood it is made of
create.ponder.hand_crank.header: Generating Rotational Force using Hand Cranks
create.ponder.hand_crank.text_1: Hand Cranks let a player turn things by hand
create.ponder.hand_crank.text_2: Keep Right-Click held down to wind it Counter-Clockwise
create.ponder.hand_crank.text_3: Hold Right-Click while Sneaking to wind it Clockwise instead
create.ponder.valve_handle.text_1: A Valve Handle turns whatever it drives by an exact angle
create.ponder.valve_handle.text_2: Set that angle by scrolling on its value panel
create.ponder.valve_handle.text_3: Right-Click it once to perform a single turn
create.ponder.valve_handle.text_4: Sneak and Right-Click to turn it back the other way
create.ponder.valve_handle.text_5: Remember to set the Bearing so that it does not disassemble when it stops
create.ponder.valve_handle.text_6: Dye a Valve Handle to change its colour
create.ponder.chain_drive.header: Relaying rotational force with Chain Drives
create.ponder.chain_drive.text_1: Chain Drives placed in a row pass rotation along to each other
create.ponder.chain_drive.text_2: Unlike cogwheels, every shaft along the chain turns in the same direction
create.ponder.chain_drive.text_3: Any drive in the row may be turned 90 degrees to point its shaft another way
create.ponder.chain_gearshift.header: Controlling rotational speed with Chain Gearshifts
create.ponder.chain_gearshift.text_1: Without power, an Adjustable Chain Gearshift works just like a normal Chain Drive
create.ponder.chain_gearshift.text_2: Powered, it doubles the speed it hands on to the other drives in the row
create.ponder.chain_gearshift.text_3: If the powered Gearshift is not where the rotation comes in, it halves its own speed instead
create.ponder.chain_gearshift.text_4: Either way, the plain Chain Drives always turn twice as fast as the powered Gearshift
create.ponder.chain_gearshift.text_5: An analog redstone signal lets you pick any ratio between 1 and 2
A Rotation Speed Controller takes the rotation running through it and drives the Large Cogwheel on top
Scroll over the value panel on its side to set the speed it hands on
create.ponder.speedometer.header: Monitoring Kinetic information using the Speedometer
create.ponder.speedometer.text_1: A Speedometer shows how fast the components it is attached to are turning
create.ponder.speedometer.text_2: Wearing Engineer's Goggles while looking at the gauge reveals its exact readings
create.ponder.speedometer.text_3: A Redstone Comparator reading the gauge gives off a signal that grows with the measured speed
create.ponder.stressometer.header: Monitoring Kinetic information using the Stressometer
create.ponder.stressometer.text_1: A Stressometer shows how much of the network's Stress Capacity is in use
create.ponder.stressometer.text_2: Wearing Engineer's Goggles while looking at the gauge reveals its exact readings
create.ponder.stressometer.text_3: A Redstone Comparator reading the gauge gives off a signal that grows with the measured stress
create.ponder.steam_engine.text_1: A Steam Engine is mounted on the side of a Fluid Tank
create.ponder.steam_engine.text_2: Use a Shaft on the engine to give it a kinetic output
create.ponder.steam_engine.text_3: Once the boiler has enough heat, water and room...
create.ponder.steam_engine.text_5: The smallest working boiler is made of 4 Fluid Tanks
create.ponder.steam_engine.text_6: Fuelled Blaze Burners underneath raise the power the boiler can deliver
create.ponder.steam_engine.text_7: Each higher power level asks for more water, a larger boiler and more heat
create.ponder.steam_engine.text_8: Look at the boiler while wearing Engineer's Goggles to see its current power level
create.ponder.steam_engine.text_9: For every power level the boiler has, one more engine can run at full strength
create.ponder.steam_whistle.text_1: A Steam Whistle goes on the side of a Fluid Tank
create.ponder.steam_whistle.text_2: Once the tank is being heated enough...
create.ponder.steam_whistle.text_3: ...it sounds a note whenever it receives a redstone signal
create.ponder.steam_whistle.text_4: Using another Whistle on it makes it longer and drops its pitch
create.ponder.steam_whistle.text_5: Use a Wrench on it to step through three octaves
create.ponder.steam_whistle.text_6: Engineer's Goggles tell you which note a Whistle is currently set to
